definition: Loyal wingman drone, also referred as a collaborative combat aircraft (CCA) or autonomous collaborative platform (ACP), is a specialized class of autonomous or semi-autonomous unmanned combat aerial vehicle (UCAV) designed to perform aerial manned-unmanned teaming and operate as a force multiplier alongside crewed fighter jets and other military aircraft.
details: Unlike traditional ground controlled remotely piloted drones, a loyal wingman controlled by utilizing human-in-the-loop from a manned aircraft and artificial intelligence (AI) of the loyal wingman drone to fly in formation, react to changing battlefield conditions, and independently execute commands without requiring constant manual inputs from a ground operator. An unmanned fighter aircraft can function equally well as a loyal wingman drone when designed for that role, but a loyal wingman drone is not always an unmanned fighter aircraft.

explainer.lead: A loyal wingman drone is an autonomous or semi-autonomous combat aircraft that flies alongside crewed fighters as a force multiplier. It shifts aerial teaming toward human-in-the-loop control with AI handling formation and reaction.

tiers.eli5: It's like a robotic teammate flying next to a piloted jet, following instructions and handling the busywork so the pilot can focus.
tiers.practitioner: Designers pair human-in-the-loop control from a crewed aircraft with onboard AI for formation flight and independent execution of commands. A pitfall is over-trusting autonomy in contested, changing battlefield conditions.
tiers.paperLevel: A specialized class of autonomous or semi-autonomous unmanned combat aerial vehicle designed for manned-unmanned teaming, operating as a force multiplier alongside crewed aircraft; unlike ground-controlled remotely piloted drones, it is controlled via human-in-the-loop from a manned aircraft plus onboard AI to fly in formation and execute commands without constant manual input.

explainer.example: A crewed fighter directs a wingman drone to hold formation and react to a changing threat, with the drone executing the command autonomously rather than via a ground operator.
